extracted.intended_audience: ICCV 2025 reviewers (and Area Chairs / Program Committee members involved in reviewing)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and enforceable policies for reviewers evaluating submissions to ICCV 2025, covering review quality, ethics, conflicts, deadlines, handling of data/code/ethics issues, and use of LLMs. Includes instructions for what to check in papers and consequences for policy violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsible Reviewing Policy (definition of highly irresponsible reviews)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are expected to provide fair and thoughtful reviews. Examples of highly irresponsible behavior include: one-sentence reviews, reviews generated by Large Language Models (LLMs), reviews that are irrelevant to the paper, or reviews that overlook substantial portions of the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a review is flagged as highly irresponsible, it will undergo an oversight process managed by the Program Chairs (PCs). Any reviewer whose review is deemed to be 'highly irresponsible' may face a desk rejection of all papers on which they are an author at the PCs' discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewing Deadline Policy (timeliness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must submit assigned reviews by the strict deadline. Failure to submit by the deadline may result in desk rejection of all papers on which the reviewer is an author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple reminder emails will be sent. Co-authors of late reviewers will be notified that their submission may be desk rejected if reviews are not submitted in time. This policy is strictly enforced to reduce organizer workload and ensure fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-blind reviewing (anonymity principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: ICCV reviewing is double blind: authors do not know ACs/reviewers and area chairs/reviewers are not told authors' names. PCs have full visibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should not take active steps to discover authors' identities; if authors are known via arXiv that's not automatically a conflict but reviewers must still be impartial. PCs cannot submit papers to ICCV 2025.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check assignments for conflicts and comfort
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon assignment, reviewers must check (a) for obvious conflicts of interest and (b) whether they feel comfortable reviewing the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If issues arise, contact the Area Chair immediately so they can reassign the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know and apply conference policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should read the Author Guidelines and be familiar with official policies authors are expected to follow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you suspect a policy violation, contact the Chairs but proceed to review the paper assuming no violation has taken place in the interim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical soundness and contribution (what to weigh)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each accepted paper should be technically sound and make a contribution to the field. Weigh novelty and potential impact alongside reported performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embrace novel, brave concepts even if tested on few datasets. Not exceeding state-of-the-art on a benchmark is not, by itself, grounds for rejection. Minor, easily corrected flaws should not be sole reasons for rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed reviews (depth and structure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews should be thoughtful and detailed; ideally formed after reflection over several days. Main critique should be presented as a list of strengths and weaknesses with explanations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short reviews tend to be enigmatic and unhelpful. Bullet lists with one short phrase per bullet are NOT detailed. The detailed review matters more than the score for helping authors, reviewers, and ACs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specificity (novelty, writing, and citations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Be specific about claims (e.g., novelty) and back them up with specific references and explanations. Be specific when suggesting writing improvements (point to sections and give suggestions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Saying 'this has been done before' must include references explaining how prior work is related. In related work discussions, cite specific publications, books, or public disclosures rather than vague statements. Missing citations or comparisons to arXiv are not sole grounds for rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive feedback to improve submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide concrete suggestions for how authors can improve their papers (technical tools, datasets, application areas, generalizations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If out of scope for ICCV, explain why and suggest other venues. Be generous with actionable ideas to help authors improve their work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone and professionalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews must be courteous, informative, incisive, and helpful. Avoid belittling or sarcastic comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid referring to authors in the second person ('you') or even 'the authors'; prefer referring to 'the paper.' A constructive tone benefits both authors and the reviewer's reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility checks (code & artifacts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are encouraged to submit code as supplementary material; reviewers may optionally check code to ensure results are reproducible and trustworthy but are not required to.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All code/data reviewed must be kept confidential and deleted after review. Accepted papers are expected (but not required) to provide accompanying code upon acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset contribution expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: If a paper claims a dataset release as a scientific contribution, the dataset is expected to be made publicly available no later than the camera-ready deadline if accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate dataset claims with the expectation of public release; private/restricted datasets can be used in experiments but cannot be claimed as a contribution in their own right.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution of data assets (cite datasets/code)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must cite data assets (datasets, code) used in the paper much like they cite papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should check whether the paper has adequately cited data assets and comment in the corresponding field in the review form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of personal data and human subjects (ethics checks)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a paper uses personal data or human-subject data, authors must have IRB or equivalent ethics clearance or clearly describe how ethical principles were followed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no description or glaring ethical violations exist, inform the Area Chairs and Program Chairs. Reviewers should not attempt to resolve ethics issues themselves. For existing published datasets, inclusion of IRB discussion is encouraged but not required and should not be penalized if absent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion of negative societal impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are encouraged to include a discussion of potential negative societal impact; reviewers should weigh its inclusion positively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lack of such a discussion is NOT grounds for rejection since there is no formal policy requiring it yet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion of limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are encouraged to explicitly and honestly discuss limitations; this should be weighed positively by reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A separate limitations section is not required and cannot be a sole factor for rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect anonymity (do not de-anonymize)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should not attempt to discover authors' identities, and should make efforts to keep their own identity invisible to authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a reviewer happens to recognize authors (e.g., via arXiv), they may still review if they can be impartial; do not search the web to find identities. If at the start you do not know identities, do not attempt to find them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect ideas and maintain confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Protect confidentiality of submitted work: do not show the paper or supplementary material to anyone outside the review process, do not use ideas from papers you review, and destroy all copies after the review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not show results, videos, images, or supplementary materials to non-reviewers. Erase any implementations or results produced while evaluating the paper after the process completes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid conflicts of interest (COI rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must avoid any conflict of interest that could question impartiality. If assigned a paper that creates a possible COI, return the paper and do not submit a review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include: same institution as an author; direct involvement in the work; recent collaboration (about 3 years); being an advisor or advisee; situations others might reasonably perceive as conflicts. If you suspect a COI, contact the Area Chair to reassign.

rubrics_metrics.name: LLM ethics for reviewers (prohibition and limited allowed uses)
rubrics_metrics.description: Large language models (LLMs) and online chatbots (e.g., ChatGPT) are NOT allowed to be used to write reviews or meta-reviews, whether local or via API. Reviewers cannot share substantial content from the paper or their review with an LLM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed uses: background research or checking short phrases for clarity; grammar-checker software based on LLMs is allowed. Reviews/meta-reviews will be checked for violations; flagged reviews enter an oversight process and confirmed violations may lead to desk rejection of the reviewer's papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of arXiv and prior work
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are not required to discuss or compare against very recent arXiv reports; failing to beat arXiv is not sole grounds for rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should properly acknowledge sources that directly and obviously inspired them. If plagiarism or academic dishonesty is suspected (e.g., same ideas, different authors), notify the Program Chairs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary material restrictions and handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplementary material is intended for derivations and results that do not fit in the main paper. It MAY NOT include results obtained with an improved version of the method or an updated/corrected submission PDF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult supplemental only if helpful to understand the paper. If you find violations in the supplementary material, contact the Area Chair.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rebuttal phase limitations (requests and allowed content)
rubrics_metrics.description: In reviews you may request clarifications, additional illustrations, or small experiments that could reasonably be run during the rebuttal phase, but you should not request substantial additional experiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Substantial' refers to what would be needed in a major revision. The rebuttal may include figures or comparison tables with results reported in the submission/supplement or other papers; reviewers should not penalize authors for supplying extra results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling withdrawn datasets
rubrics_metrics.description: Using a withdrawn dataset (e.g., DukeMTMC-ReID) is not by itself grounds for rejection, but should invite close scrutiny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag such cases to ACs and PCs. Consider whether authors explain why they used the withdrawn dataset and whether acceptable alternatives exist. If the paper could be accepted without those experiments, advise authors to remove them. It is a violation for reviewers/ACs to require comparisons on withdrawn datasets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison requests to closed-source prior work
rubrics_metrics.description: When requesting comparisons to published research without publicly available code/data (requiring re-implementation), reviewers must appropriately justify such requests if they are to be used as a basis for a paper decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: minor changes to an already implemented method whose code/data is available, or re-implementation is standard practice in a sub-field. In any case, request comparisons only if the publication/code has been available sufficiently ahead of the submission deadline, per 2024 PAMI-TC motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences for policy violations (enforcement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy violations such as highly irresponsible reviews, LLM policy breaches, or missing strict deadlines can result in oversight processes and may lead to desk rejection of all papers on which the offending reviewer is an author, at the PCs' discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Area Chairs may assign emergency reviewers when needed. PCs make final enforcement decisions.
